title: Polymorphic deployment profiles for environment-specific canaries, A/B, shadowing and auto-rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We need a single authoring surface for model rollout policies (canary, A/B, shadow) that compiles to environment-specific runtime configs for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Current approach duplicates policies per environment and requires ad-hoc compatibility shims (e.g., different ingress rules, RBAC, KMS references, and autoscaler knobs). This ticket proposes a polymorphic deployment profile layer ("profile compiler") that maps high-level rollout intents to concrete environment artifacts, enforces constraints, and injects safe defaults for things that differ across environments.
acceptance_criteria: Author a rollout using the polymorph profile DSL and successfully deploy a canary that routes 5% traffic on Hosted with standard prefix-caching enabled
Same DSL compiles to a Dedicated deployment manifest that provisions canary pool and respects tenant isolation (no shared KV cache)
Private/VPC compilation substitutes customer KMS references and disables cross-tenant shadowing by default
Auto-rollback rules are enforced at the policy runner and trigger a rollback in a simulated failure test (SLO breach or error-rate spike)
Console shows per-environment compiled diffs and the rollout plan, with links to the generated runtime manifests
E2E tests run in CI covering canary promote/fail flows for Hosted and Dedicated (Private simulated)
No performance regressions in 95th percentile latency vs current rollout controller (within 5%)
tasks: Design polymorph DSL and schema (API + YAML) - draft spec
Implement compiler component that emits Hosted/Dedicated/Private manifests
Integrate policy runner to read compiled manifests and manage traffic splits (canary/A-B/shadow)
Add auto-rollback hooks into runtime SLO guard with configurable thresholds
Console: display compiled artifacts and allow vault/KMS link review
Write CI e2e tests including a synthetic failure to validate rollback
Create migration tool for existing rollouts to be re-authorable via the DSL
Documentation: authoring guide, examples, and troubleshooting notes
decision_log: 2025-11-21: Chose polymorph approach instead of multiple authoring UIs to reduce drift and maintenance cost - decided by PM, Infra, and Runtime leads
2025-11-27: Agreed that Dedicated will default to isolated KV caches and stronger rolling windows due to predictable capacity
2025-11-30: Private builds will require customer-provided secrets for KMS and will disable tenant-level shadowing by default for compliance
2025-12-03: Auto-rollback will be implemented in the policy runner as an external action rather than baked into the serving runtime to allow heterogeneous runtime integrations
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Divergent compiled manifests could still allow subtle behavior differences across environments. Mitigation: compile-time diff tool and nightly parity checks between Hosted/Dedicated testbeds.

Risk: Private deployments may not support certain dynamic features (e.g., autoscaling hooks). Mitigation: the compiler will emit capability constraints and a baked-in fallback (static pool) where autoscaling hooks are unavailable.
Risk: Incorrect auto-rollback thresholds could cause flapping. Mitigation: conservative defaults + canary ramp delay + synthetic test harness in CI
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Implement DSL + compiler and run internal smoke tests (Hosted only). Phase 2: Integrate policy runner with Hosted canaries and enable auto-rollback in a staged rollout (internal teams). Phase 3: Add Dedicated compiler mapping and run capacity-aware canary experiments. Phase 4: Partner with 1-2 pilot customers for Private deployment verification. Monitor telemetry and enable parity gates (diff checks) before wider release.
testing_plan: Unit tests for compiler transformations per environment
Integration tests: policy runner + serving runtime with synthetic traffic patterns
E2E CI job: deploy example canary, simulate SLO failure, validate rollback
Nightly parity job: compile same DSL to all environments and run smoke tests in sandbox clusters
